title: Compassion
definition: Compassion is heartfelt concern that moves a person toward those who are hurting, needy, weak, suffering, or vulnerable with practical love and care.
summary: Compassion is more than feeling sorry for someone. Biblical compassion moves believers to action. God calls His people to notice suffering, respond with kindness, and serve others in ways that reflect His heart. Compassion should shape how Christians interact with the poor, the sick, the grieving, the disabled, the lonely, and the hurting.
christFocus: Jesus consistently demonstrated compassion through His words, actions, healing, teaching, and sacrificial love.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Without compassion, doctrine can become cold and disconnected from real life. Understanding God's compassion helps believers reflect His character to a hurting world.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Pay attention to the needs around you. Ask God to help you see people through His eyes. Look for practical ways to encourage, serve, support, and care for those who are hurting.
